Another remote possibility is that vehicle design changes, i.e., engine recalibration, transmission adjustments, etc., made by manufacturers to increase fuel economy might affect the deterioration rate of the emission control system. Conceivably, while the emission level of a vehicle could be below the standard at 50,000 miles, the emission of the redesigned vehicle at more than 50,000 miles could be greater or less than the unchanged vehicle. Again, NHTSA does not have data to quantify this effect but the possible effect on air quality should be minimal.
AFES could have an impact due to the decreased use of cast iron and steel and the increased use of aluminum and plastics. If the changes to the environment are proportional to the changes in use of these materials, the impact should be minor as the increase in the use of these materials is very small.
